heard: The first confirmed black hole shoots, jets at half-light speed. Discovered in 1964 during a sounding rocket flight, Cygnus X-1 sits 7,000 light years away. This heavy weight is locked in a tight celestial tango with a massive blue supergiant star. They orbit every 5.6 days, at just one-fifth, the distance between the Earth and Sun. The black hole continuously rips material from its companion, forming a disk that blazes in x-rays. But the record-breaking surprise is the twin plasma jets blasting from the center. These blazing jets shine with the energy of 10,000 suns while visibly dancing across space. Stellar winds from the supergiant make these beams visibly wobble as they race away.
